PullRequest.Title: Identify GitHub GraphQL requests with the VS Code version
PullRequest.Body:
Identify the built-in GitHub extension's GraphQL requests as `vscode.github/<VS Code version>`, using the version shipped with the application rather than the extension manifest's placeholder.

Register the GitHub extension suite with the maintained integration runners so its transport regression tests run in CI. This also corrects the previously dormant smoke test's fixture-relative path calculation.

Closes https://github.com/github/graphql-platform/issues/5142

Authored by Copilot, guided by @jidicula.

Scenarios.Scenario: GitHub-backed branch protection and source-control history queries create or reuse the GraphQL client, then issue GraphQL requests.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold client, authentication session lookup and the dynamic Octokit import complete before the first GraphQL network request; warm calls reuse `_octokitGraphql`. The PR adds only user-agent header construction to that existing path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Look up the silent GitHub authentication session through the VS Code authentication API.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lookup on cold client creation or after session invalidation; warm client access performs none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The method directly called the same `authentication.getSession('github', scopes, { silent: true })`; the diff delegates through a default function without changing cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only cold GraphQL client creation before a query can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue GitHub GraphQL queries for repository details, rulesets, assignable users, or commit authors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged: one request per existing query, plus existing sequential pagination for rulesets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same queries and request counts were sent without the VS Code-version user-agent value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Feature results wait for their existing GraphQL requests; the new constant-size user-agent header does not add another request or round trip.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: GraphQL request count still scales with repositories, requested history details, and ruleset pagination. The added user-agent is constant-size per request and does not change request cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `@sequentialize` continues to serialize cold client creation. Query concurrency and ruleset pagination behavior are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The positive GraphQL-client cache remains one client per `OctokitService`, invalidated on GitHub authentication-session changes and disposal. Failed or absent-session initialization remains uncached and retryable; the injected default calls the same authentication API with the same options.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed initialization, cache field, invalidation listener, and all repository callers were traced; no extra lookup or network call is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact query volume and network latency vary by repositories and usage, but the diff's added bytes and CPU are constant per already-existing request.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Client lifetime, request fan-out, and critical-path boundaries are unchanged; the required header adds negligible bounded serialization/network bytes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Unfiltered or explicitly selected integration runs execute the newly registered GitHub extension suite.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For an unfiltered integration run, earlier suites complete before `npm run test-extension -- -l github` launches and finishes; an explicit `--suite github` run executes only this suite. The suite activates the extension, performs a fixed fixture template scan and UI tests, and uses mocked fetch for the two new GraphQL tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the GitHub extension test runner/Electron extension host via `npm run test-extension -- -l github`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one added launch in each unfiltered integration run or matching suite-selected run; the Linux, macOS, and Windows CI jobs each invoke their platform script when enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The integration scripts did not invoke the GitHub suite, so these tests had no extension-host launch in maintained integration runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds the bounded suite duration to the sequential integration-test job, intentionally placing the previously dormant transport regression tests on CI's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover pull-request-template files in the fixed `extensions/github/testWorkspace` fixture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scan of the fixed fixture per suite execution, returning nine templates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test existed but was not registered with these maintained integration runners.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs within the added suite before that test completes; it is bounded by the checked-in fixture.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exercise GraphQL requests using an injected fetch implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two in-process mocked fetch calls in one test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These user-agent tests did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No external network I/O; responses are constructed synchronously in process.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One extra suite launch per unfiltered integration-script invocation on each selected CI platform; test cardinality is fixed at five tests in the GitHub test directory, not proportional to repository or user data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The scripts run extension suites sequentially. The new suite adds one sequential extension-host launch rather than an aggregate concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The runner disables cached data and uses the integration run's temporary user-data directory. The GraphQL test verifies one cached client and uses an in-process mocked fetch; there is no cold/warm external network cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: suite selection logic, all three CI entry points, test inventory, and mocked network path were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual Electron startup time varies by CI host, but multiplicity is fixed at one added sequential suite launch per integration invocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance bug. The bounded sequential subprocess cost is the intentional cost of registering the suite for regression coverage, with no accidental duplication or input-scaled fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: The GitHub smoke test normalizes discovered fixture paths before sorting and assertion.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing filesystem discovery completes, nine returned URI paths are mapped through `path.posix.relative`, sorted, and compared.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing discovery operation over the fixed workspace fixture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery ran before the diff; only string slicing was replaced by path-relative normalization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The test waits for discovery before path normalization; the changed normalization itself crosses no boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU work is linear in the number of discovered templates, which is nine in the fixed test fixture.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous in-process mapping and sorting after one asynchronous discovery; no changed concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; the operation runs once in its test.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete test and changed expression were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material because the checked-in fixture is fixed and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Replacing slice with `path.posix.relative` adds only trivial bounded CPU in test code and no new boundary work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and their runtime/test call paths. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced; no findings or regression-fix records were submitted.
